setting.title: Murder at Ashford Manor
setting.eraNote: A wet October weekend. The family and two guests are gathered for Lord Ashford's sixtieth birthday.

locations.label: The Study
locations.description: Lord Ashford's private study, where he was found slumped over his desk.

locations.label: The Library
locations.description: Tall shelves, a card table, and a dying fire.

locations.label: The Garden & Potting Shed
locations.description: Rain-soaked lawns leading to the gardener's potting shed.

locations.label: The Kitchen
locations.description: The servants' domain, still warm from the evening's supper.

locations.label: The Guest Wing
locations.description: Bedrooms for family and visitors along the east corridor.

briefing: Lord Edmund Ashford took his customary brandy alone in his study at ten o'clock. By half past, he was dead. The local doctor smells garlic on his lips: arsenic. The roads are flooded, nobody has left the house, and the Chief Constable wants a name by morning.

motive.text: Henry learned at tea that afternoon that his uncle was cutting him out of the will.

motiveOptions.label: About to be cut out of the will
An unpaid loan between old friends

truthTimeline.event: Told by Lord Ashford at tea that he will be cut out of the will
Starts a game of bridge with Lady Margaret in the library
Slips out to the potting shed and takes arsenic weed killer
Crosses the wet lawn back to the house, seen from the kitchen window
Goes to the kitchen to cadge supper from Mrs. Pell
Doctors the brandy decanter in the empty study
Changes out of muddy shoes in the guest wing

suspects.name: Lady Margaret Ashford
suspects.personality: Cool, precise, aristocratic; hides worry behind impeccable manners.
suspects.appearance: Grey silk, a single strand of pearls that are not quite real.
suspects.alibiClaim: I spent the whole evening at bridge in the library with Dr. Finch.

claimedTimeline.event: Bridge with Dr. Finch in the library until after half past ten

knows: At tea, Edmund told Henry he would be cut out of the will. Henry stormed out.
Edmund had been unwell and irritable for weeks.
Dr. Finch and Edmund had argued by letter recently.
suspects.motiveHint: The estate is less wealthy than it appears.

secrets.text: She secretly pawned the family pearls to pay household bills.
secrets.confession: Very well. The pearls I wear are paste. I pawned the real ones in Bath to keep this house running. Edmund never knew.

lies.text: Claims the family has no money troubles
lies.statement: Money? The Ashfords have never had to think about money.

suspects.name: Henry Ashford
suspects.personality: Charming, quick with a joke, turns sharp and defensive when money or the will comes up.
suspects.appearance: A pale linen dinner jacket and a too-ready smile.
suspects.alibiClaim: I was in the library reading all evening.

claimedTimeline.event: Reading in the library all evening

knows: Uncle Edmund told him at tea that he was to be cut out of the will.
The gardener keeps arsenic weed killer in the potting shed.

secrets.text: He owes a great deal of money to dangerous men in London from gambling.
secrets.confession: All right! I owe money to some rather unpleasant fellows in London. Cards. It's hardly a crime.

lies.text: Claims he was in the library all evening
lies.statement: I was in the library reading all evening.

lies.text: Claims he never went to the garden
lies.statement: I never set foot in the garden tonight. In this rain? Hardly.

lies.text: Claims he didn't know about the will change
lies.statement: Uncle's will? I had no idea he meant to change anything.

suspects.name: Mrs. Agnes Pell
suspects.personality: Brisk, loyal, a little sharp-tongued, proud of thirty years' service.
suspects.appearance: Black dress, starched apron, keys at her waist.
suspects.alibiClaim: I was in my kitchen from supper until midnight, as always.
knows: Around a quarter to ten she saw a figure in a pale jacket cross the lawn from the potting shed toward the garden door.
Colonel Hayes came down to the kitchen for supper around ten to ten and stayed chatting until half past.
suspects.motiveHint: Lord Ashford had threatened to pension her off.

secrets.text: She has been quietly drinking from the master's wine cellar for years.
secrets.confession: Oh, have it your way. A glass from the cellar now and then. Thirty years I've given this house. A glass of claret is hardly theft.

lies.text: Claims she never touches the cellar
lies.statement: I would never touch the master's cellar. Never.

suspects.name: Dr. Julian Finch
suspects.personality: Smooth, clinical, condescending; sweats when his professional reputation is questioned.
suspects.appearance: Tweed suit, gold pince-nez, a doctor's bag never far away.
suspects.alibiClaim: Bridge in the library with Lady Margaret, from half past nine.

claimedTimeline.event: Bridge with Lady Margaret in the library

knows: Lord Ashford showed classic signs of arsenic poisoning.
Nobody else came into the library during the bridge game, from half past nine to twenty to eleven.
suspects.motiveHint: Lord Ashford threatened to report him to the Medical Council.

secrets.text: He has been over-prescribing laudanum to Lady Margaret, and Edmund threatened to report him.
secrets.confession: Edmund found out about the laudanum prescriptions. He threatened to write to the Council. But I did not kill him, Inspector. I was at cards the whole night.

lies.text: Claims he and Edmund were on the best of terms
lies.statement: Edmund and I were the best of friends. Never a cross word.

suspects.name: Colonel Reginald Hayes
suspects.personality: Bluff, loud, old-fashioned; blusters when cornered.
suspects.appearance: Regimental tie, a magnificent moustache, frayed cuffs.
suspects.alibiClaim: Went down to the kitchen for a spot of supper, then turned in.
knows: He saw Henry in the guest wing corridor around a quarter past ten, carrying his shoes.
Edmund and Henry had a shouting match at tea.
suspects.motiveHint: Owed Lord Ashford a large sum.

secrets.text: He is broke and came to beg Edmund for more time on a £2,000 loan.
secrets.confession: Dash it all. I'm stony broke. I came to ask Edmund for more time on the loan. Hardly a reason to kill the man who might give it to me.

lies.text: Claims Edmund owed him money, not the other way round
lies.statement: Money between us? If anything, Edmund owed me, old boy.

clues.title: Muddy shoes
clues.text: In Henry's room in the guest wing: a pair of evening shoes caked with fresh garden mud and pushed under the bed.

clues.title: The Colonel's IOU
clues.text: In the Colonel's room: an IOU for £2,000, signed 'R. Hayes' and made out to Lord Ashford.

clues.title: Letter to the solicitor
clues.text: On the study desk, an unfinished letter in Lord Ashford's hand: 'Henry is to receive nothing. I told him so myself this afternoon.'

clues.title: The brandy decanter
clues.text: The decanter smells faintly of garlic. One glass used, one clean. Whoever poisoned it knew he always drank alone at ten.

clues.title: Weed killer tin
clues.text: In the potting shed, a tin of arsenic weed killer with its lid freshly prised open. Wet footprints lead back toward the house.

clues.title: Hidden bottles
clues.text: Under the scullery sink: three empty bottles from the master's cellar, carefully hidden.

clues.title: Pawn ticket
clues.text: Tucked inside a book of sermons in the library: a Bath pawnbroker's ticket for 'one pearl necklace', signed M. Ashford.

clues.title: Figure on the lawn
clues.text: Mrs. Pell saw a figure in a pale jacket cross from the potting shed to the garden door at about a quarter to ten.

timelineEvent.event: A figure in a pale jacket crosses from the shed (Mrs. Pell's sighting)

clues.title: Quarrel at tea
clues.text: Lady Margaret: at tea, Edmund told Henry he would be cut out of the will. Henry went white and stormed out.

timelineEvent.event: Told at tea he is cut out of the will

clues.title: Torn letter
clues.text: Dr. Finch drops a torn note: '...cannot keep silent about your prescriptions any longer. E.A.'

clues.title: Henry's admission
clues.text: Cornered, Henry admits he walked to the potting shed at about twenty to ten, 'for a smoke'.

timelineEvent.event: At the potting shed (his own admission)

clues.title: The bridge game
clues.text: Dr. Finch's score card: he and Lady Margaret played bridge in the library from 21:30 to 22:40, and no one else came in.

timelineEvent.event: Bridge in the library with Lady Margaret until 22:40, nobody else present

clues.title: Supper in the kitchen
clues.text: The Colonel and Mrs. Pell vouch for each other: he ate supper in the kitchen from 21:50 until 22:30.

timelineEvent.event: Supper in the kitchen with Mrs. Pell until 22:30
